After Waterloo, parts of France were held by foreign armies for years, and France paid for it. This map shows who held what in 1815.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The Second Treaty of Paris was signed on 20 November 1815, after Napoleon's Hundred Days ended at Waterloo. It was far harsher than the treaty of 1814.
2/ France was cut back to roughly its 1790 borders, plus a few enclaves, and had to pay 700 million francs in indemnities, in five yearly instalments.

3/ It also had to host a coalition army of up to 150,000 soldiers in its eastern border regions, at French expense. The map splits the north and east into British, Prussian, Russian, Austrian and smaller German zones.
4/ The occupation was set for up to five years but ended after three. The coalition troops left in 1818, once the Duke of Wellington judged the occupation no longer necessary.
5/ Counting interest and the upkeep of the troops, the total burden approached 1.7 billion francs, described as the heaviest war reparation ever paid relative to GDP (per Wikipedia).
Would a gentler peace have worked better? Debate it below. Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
